Algorithm:
- Use loop var i that runs from len(l)-1 to 1, decrementing by 1 
in each itr. This loop tracks curr pos in list.
- Within outer loop, use another loop var j that runs from 0 to i-1. 
This loop traverses unsorted part of list.
- Compare adj ele l[j] and l[j+1]. If l[j] is greater than l[j+1], 
swap them to put smaller element first.
- Repeat process until the entire list is sorted, with each pass 
pushing the next largest element to its correct position.
- Return sorted list l
Time & Space Complexity:
Worst, Average and 
Best case: O(n^2)

Algorithm:
- Use loop var i that runs from 0 to len(l)-2 to track curr pos 
in list that needs sorting.
- Set min_index to i. This var keeps track of index of the min ele 
found in unsorted part of the list.
- Within outer loop, use another loop var j that runs from 
i+1 to len(l)-1 to traverse the unsorted part of the list.
- Compare ele l[min_index] and l[j]. If l[j] is smaller than l[min_index], 
update min_index to j.
- After inner loop completes, swap ele at index i with ele at min_index.
- Repeat this process until the entire list is sorted.
- Return sorted list l
Time & Space Complexity:
Worst, Average and 
Best case: O(n^2)

Algorithm:
- Use loop var i that runs from 1 to len(l)-1 to iterate list starting 
from second ele.
- Set key to l[i]. This var stores curr ele to be inserted in its 
correct position.
- Set j to i-1. This var is used to traverse sorted portion of the list.
- While j is greater than or equal to 0 and l[j] is greater than key:
    - Move l[j] one position to the right, i.e., set l[j + 1] to l[j].
    - Decrement j by 1.
- Insert the key at position j + 1.
- Repeat this process until entire list is sorted.
- Return sorted list l.
Time & Space Complexity:
Worst and Average: 
O(n^2)
Best case:
O(n)
